newsitem.title: USA: Proxima sees fiscal 1998 near break-even.
newsitem.headline: Proxima sees fiscal 1998 near break-even.

text.p: Proxima Corp on Monday said it will work on new product offerings to help boost what it expects will be near break-even earnings in fiscal 1998, ending in March next year.

"While we expect fiscal year 1998 to be near break-even, we intend to use our financial strength to fund new best-in-class products, leverage our strength in distribution and seek new market opportunities for our projectors," Proxima said in a statement.
Earlier, the company reported a net loss of $1.10 a share after charges for the fourth quarter of fiscal 1997.

The fourth quarter included charges of $5.0 million for inventory write-offs and $1.8 million for a company-wide restructuring. Absent the charges, the company would have lost $0.16 a share compared with a profit of $0.47 a share in the fourth quarter one year ago.
Fourth quarter sales topped $36 million versus $47.6 million one year ago.
For all of fiscal 1997, Proxima reported a net loss of $1.36 a share on sales of $155 million compared with a profit of $1.37 a share on sales of $160 million in fiscal 1996.

Proxima, a maker of portable, easy-to-use projectors and project display panels for meeting presentations, cited increased competition as hurting gross margins across product lines. Also, rapidly evolving technologies have resulted in shorter product life cycles, reduceing the revenue windows of our new product offerings.
